title: Find the weekday of any date in your head
description:
4/4, 6/6, 8/8, 10/10 and 12/12 always share a weekday (each is exactly 9 weeks after the last), and so do 5/9, 9/5, 7/11 and 11/7. In 2026 they're all Saturdays, so Christmas is a Friday. For any other year, take the last two digits, add a quarter of them rounded down, drop the sevens and count on from the century's day (1900s Wednesday, 2000s Tuesday): 69 + 17 = 86, 2 left, so 1969's day is Friday and 20 July 1969, the Moon landing, was a Sunday. January's day is the 3rd (the 4th in leap years), February's the last day, March's the 14th. This is John Conway's Doomsday rule (1973).

Numbers checked in code: the method gives the right weekday for all 146,097 dates from 1800 to 2199. Source: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doomsday_rule

beats.say: These five dates always fall on the same weekday.
April 4th, June 6th, August 8th, October 10th, December 12th. Every year. Each is exactly 9 weeks after the last.
This year, they're all Saturdays. That's your anchor day.
Odd months? I work 9 to 5 at the 7-Eleven. May 9th, September 5th, July 11th, November 7th. Saturdays too.
So, Christmas. December 12th is a Saturday. Add a week: the 19th, the 26th. The 25th is a Friday.
That's this year. The real trick works for any year.
Take the last two digits. For 1969, that's 69. Add a quarter, rounded down: 17. That's 86. Throw away sevens: 2 left.
The 1900s start on Wednesday. Two days on: Friday.
July 11th is a Friday, so the 18th is, and the 20th is a Sunday. Apollo 11 landed on the Moon on a Sunday.
The 2000s start on Tuesday. So what weekday were you born on?
